subject: Sapphire: priority bridge for tenant-residency + reserved SLA lane
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Tsu <emma@sapphire.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sapphire: priority bridge for tenant-residency + reserved SLA lane

Team —

Sapphire just moved to LOI and finance is asking for a firm activation timeline tied to a reserved SLA lane and per-tenant residency for their production environment. Their legal is almost done (attached SOW draft) and they expect activation before the end of June to hit a Q3 launch commitment.

High level ask: can Product + Eng evaluate scope and give a prioritization decision on the following two items by EOD Tuesday?

1) Tenant-residency reservation (soft guarantee): ability to pin a small pool (20–40 GPUs equivalent) for Sapphire with predictable latency SLOs and a fallback plan to compatible quantized variants.
2) Per-tenant KV/prefix caching isolation: ensure their warm cache isn't evicted by noisy tenants and allow cache pre-seeding during onboarding.

Why urgent: Sapphire has signaled that reserved capacity + observable cache isolation are procurement gating items. They are planning a PO for an annual reserved commitment that would be a $1.2M ARR deal. We can negotiate phased delivery but need a clear prioritization + rough ETA to include in the mutual action plan (attached).

Attached: Sapphire_MAP_v3.pdf, SOW_Sapphire_draft.docx

Proposed tradeoffs we can consider:
- Phase 1 (by end of June): soft-residency (best-effort reserved lanes), lightweight cache pre-seeding API.
- Phase 2 (by end of Q3): hard reservation with telemetry & canary routing and SLA credits.

Next steps I'd like:
- Product: feasibility note + rough dev estimate (low/medium/high) by Tue EOD (Monica).
- Eng: early signal on thread whether this is achievable in the timeline or requires backfill (Jordan).
- Sales: I'll coordinate the MAP and sync PO timing with Sapphire (Sean).

Emma — looping you so Sapphire sees the tradeoffs early. If you have any absolutes we should know now, call them out.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

---

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Tsu <emma@sapphire.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sapphire: priority bridge for tenant-residency + reserved SLA lane

Thanks Marcus — quick read through and initial questions:

- Clarify "reserved SLA lane": do they need absolute capacity isolation (hard guarantee) or a priority queue + credits model that guarantees latency under defined load?
- Expected RPS and avg payload size for their production traffic? Helps size cache/residency needs.
- Is the PO conditional on the hard reservation being live by end of June or would a phased commitment (soft reservation then hard later) suffice?

From product perspective, we can scope a phased approach:
- Phase A: policy-based priority lanes + per-tenant tagging for routing (works with current runtime). Low dev cost but weaker guarantees.
- Phase B: dedicated residency pool + telemetry and billing changes (higher cost and infra work).

Jordan — tagging policy + cache namespace isolation are small infra changes (I think) but hard reservation + billing/SLA integration touches infra and billing. Need your estimate.

Marcus — can you push the Sapphire expected traffic numbers and confirm whether they need the hard guarantee for procurement?

Monica
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Emma Tsu <emma@sapphire.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sapphire: priority bridge for tenant-residency + reserved SLA lane

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Sapphire just moved to LOI ...

Quick engineering readout after an informal sync with infra:

- Cache isolation: we can implement a namespaced cache eviction policy + token-based pre-seed API in ~2 sprints (4 weeks) if we scope it to LRU namespace partitioning and an admin API to pre-warm keys. Low risk.
- Priority lanes / soft-residency: we can add tenant tags and priority routing with graceful degradation to compatible model variants in ~1 sprint (2 weeks). This yields meaningful latency improvements under contention but is not a strict capacity reservation.
- Hard reservation (dedicated pool + SLA credits): requires allocator + billing pipeline changes + rollout plan. Ballpark: 8–12 weeks with a small infra subproject and up to 2 FTEs from runtime to handle eviction/affinity.

Risks/notes:
- We need precise expected QPS and percentiles to size the reserved pool. Overprovisioning reduces ROI for the customer; underprovisioning risks SLA breaches.
- Billing/contracting changes: legal & Finance need to be included for SLA credits model.

Proposed suggestion for negotiation: offer Phase A (cache isolation + tagging) as our commitment in MAP, with a lined-up roadmap slot for hard reservation by end of Q3. That keeps us aligned with product velocity while giving Sapphire a path to a hard guarantee if they convert.

I'll put a short implementation notes doc in the product folder — give me 48 hours to spell out ETA and FTE count.

Jordan
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Tsu <emma@sapphire.ai>, contracts@sapphire.ai
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sapphire: priority bridge for tenant-residency + reserved SLA lane

Everyone —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. This is a high-impact deal (SAPH-2027-001) and legal is expecting our MAP language to clearly state delivery commitments. A few pragmatic asks from Sales/Rev Ops: 

- Marcus: push Emma for the QPS and 99th percentile latency targets — we need numbers we can put in the SOW.
- Monica/Jordan: Phase A + a committed roadmap slot for Hard Reservation by end of Q3 is acceptable to Sales, provided we attach a measurable acceptance criteria for Phase A (e.g., "cache pre-seed API with X keys and documented eviction policy").
- Finance: when you draft the final SOW, include a clause for SLA credits tied to the Hard Reservation milestone. We won't promise credits until we can size the pool and run a canary.

Emma — confirming: if we commit to Phase A now and deliver Phase B by end of Q3, will Sapphire sign the PO (we're expecting $1.2M ARR)? Please reply with an explicit yes/no so Marcus can update the MAP.

Also attaching the working DocuSign placeholder: https://docusign.net/sandbox/doc/abc123

I'll set up a 30-min cross-functional sync Wed to finalize acceptance criteria. Calendar invite to follow.

—Sean
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

On Wed, May 26, 2027 at 11:05 AM Emma Tsu <emma@sapphire.ai> wrote:
> Marcus / Sean / Monica / Jordan —
> 
> Thanks for the clear breakdown. We can accept a phased approach if Phase A includes cache pre-seed + documented eviction behavior and if Phase B is scoped and calendarized in the MAP. We will sign if those conditions are met.
> 
> Emma Tsu
> Head of Platform | Sapphire.ai
> emma@sapphire.ai
>
